note: NOT a regmap file. Added per team-lead's acceptance-test addendum (credited to rpi-soc's inventory). TIMERAWL/H are kind-7 counter (pure derivation from virtual cycles), but ALARMn is the design doc's WDT pattern: 'expiry is a time-triggered global side effect attached to no access at all' -- alarm match must raise an IRQ (cm0_set_irq) with no corresponding register access at the moment it fires. That side effect is what routes the whole peripheral to coded: despite TIMERAWL/H alone being pure-on-read.
why_this_matters: This is NOT a status-bit spin like the others in this deliverable -- it's a different hang class. pico-sdk's delay()/sleep_ms() blocks via a hardware alarm IRQ, not by polling a register (per the original brief: 'delay() uses a timer alarm interrupt, not polling'). A frozen or non-interrupting TIMER hangs sleep_ms() forever even with every other register in this floor correctly modeled -- so TIMER is on the critical path for anything beyond a busy-loop-only blink, and is required if the acceptance test (runtime_init() completing, plus any firmware that calls sleep_ms/delay) is to pass.
registers_not_individually_verified_this: TIMERAWL/TIMERAWH (free-running 64-bit microsecond counter, split into two 32-bit halves) -- offsets not grepped this session; referenced by name (`timer->timerawl`) in src/rp2_common/hardware_timer/timer.c's timer_busy_wait_us_32()/timer_busy_wait_until() (fetched this session, offsets 77-123 of that file), confirming the register exists and is read directly for busy-wait, but exact byte offsets within TIMER's register block were not individually extracted.

ALARM0-3 (compare registers, one per hardware alarm -- NUM_ALARMS=4 per platform_defs.h, fetched this session), INTE/INTF/INTS (interrupt enable/force/status) -- present in the TIMER block per standard RP2040 layout, not itemized this session.
confirmed_this_session: src/rp2_common/hardware_timer/timer.c (pico-sdk, fetched this session, full 295-line file read for busy-wait functions): timer_busy_wait_us_32() at line 77 does `while (timer->timerawl - start < delay_us) { tight_loop_contents(); }` -- a POLLING busy-wait, distinct from the alarm-IRQ path.

hardware_alarm_claim()/timer_hardware_alarm_claim() (timer.c:21-53, fetched this session) manage a claimed-alarm bitmap -- confirms alarms are a shared resource pico-sdk's SDK-level sleep_ms()/alarm_pool machinery arbitrates, though the IRQ-delivery callback path itself (alarm_callbacks array, timer.c:14) was not traced through to sleep_ms()'s exact call chain this session.
NUM_ALARMS=4, NUM_GENERIC_TIMERS=1 -- src/rp2040/hardware_regs/include/hardware/platform_defs.h:35-36 (pico-sdk, fetched this session). VERIFIED.
recommendation: Model TIMERAWL/H by lazy derivation from cm0_cycles() at read time (per design doc SS3: 'Vendor-side counters polled in delay loops are computed lazily from cm0_cycles at read time: one FFI trip per read, no per-tick work'), and model ALARMn match as a coded-side comparison against the derived counter value that calls cm0_set_irq() when crossed -- exactly the WDT-shaped write-clause case the design doc names as the reason WDTs (and by the same reasoning, this) route to coded: with no schema growth.
